# LifePower Control v0.1.0

This is the first public release of LifePower Control, a local-first web
application for owners of supported LiFePO4wered/Pi+ boards.

The production package targets 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS on ARM64. It includes
the controller, bounded job runner, optional loopback-only web service,
systemd integration, exact-version installer and uninstaller, SHA-256
checksums, an SPDX SBOM, and GitHub artifact attestations.

Read the installation, safety, recovery, and release-verification guides
before installing. Register changes are temporary in this release; controller
flash persistence is deliberately excluded. Raspberry Pi OS ARMv7 and generic
AMD64 systems are not production release targets.

## Supported systems and prerequisites

- Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit Trixie is the primary supported operating
  system; 64-bit Bookworm is retained as a legacy compatibility target.
- The production archive is Linux ARM64 only.
- A supported LiFePO4wered/Pi+ board and the manufacturer's standard daemon
  and `/usr/local/bin/lifepo4wered-cli` installation are required.

## Configuration, state, and rollback

This is the first public release, so there is no migration from an earlier
public version. Durable state uses schema 1. The installer preserves
configuration, authentication, controller state, Activity, job definitions,
and job output during a compatible upgrade or ordinary uninstall. Downgrade
requires an explicit flag and two-way schema compatibility. A failed upgrade
restores the previous package payload and service lifecycle; it cannot undo
external hardware changes or restore a release whose schema is incompatible.

## Security and permissions

The service runs under a locked `lifepowerctl` account. Saved jobs run as the
ordinary owner-selected account and inherit that account's existing authority;
they are not a hostile-code sandbox. A dedicated root helper is limited to the
validated orderly-poweroff request. The web listener remains on loopback and
should be reached locally or through SSH. No separate security fix is claimed
for this initial release.

## Hardware-affecting behavior

The application can make reviewed temporary register changes, program a
verified wake, run an ordered job list, and request orderly poweroff when an
enabled duty cycle reaches its accepted boundary. It fails safe on uncertain
state and leaves the Pi powered for owner review. It never invokes `CFG_WRITE`;
temporary register changes are not committed to controller flash.
